title: Real-Time Voice Cloning Ships, Perplexity Goes Agentic on Windows, and AI Labs Go Book Shopping
tldr: Fish Audio's new S2.1 Pro clones any voice live in conversation, backed by $52M in fresh seed funding.
Perplexity's agentic Computer tool now runs on Windows across Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, with a multi-model Model Council including Kimi K3.
A judge ruled Anthropic's book-buy-then-scan training approach is fair use, and bulk buyers are now cleaning out used bookstores of pre-2022 titles.

tips.heading: Record a reusable Claude skill from any repeat task
steps: Open the Claude desktop app → Cowork, click + → Record a skill, grant screen recording permissions, and click Start Recording.
Perform the task once, start to finish, narrating it out loud using the template below.
Claude packages the narration into a saved skill you can run later with /your-skill-name, or ask it to schedule the skill to run automatically.
tips.prompt:
I'm doing [TASK] to achieve [GOAL].
First, I [ACTION] because [REASON].
Next, I [ACTION] so that [OUTCOME].
If [CONDITION] happens, I [ALTERNATIVE ACTION].
This is the most important rule: [RULE OR DECISION].
Ignore any clicks or tabs that aren't part of this workflow.
When the task is complete, verify that [SUCCESS CRITERIA].

tips.heading: Use Claude to dispute an inflated medical bill
steps: Upload a photo or PDF of the itemized bill to Claude.
Ask it to flag duplicated, miscoded, or inconsistent line items.
Have it draft a dispute letter citing the discrepancies.
Send it to the provider or insurer and follow up.

news.body: Fish Audio launched S2.1 Pro, a voice model that clones any voice and speaks in it live during a conversation. The one-year-old startup has built a 2M+ voice community library, hit $21M in annual recurring revenue, and just raised $52M in seed funding.
news.means: Real-time voice cloning is now demo-ready, not a lab curiosity. Add voice-verification steps to any process that still authorizes by phone, and flag the fraud risk to clients running call centers.

news.body: Perplexity's agentic "Computer" tool now works with local files on Windows, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, and gained a "Model Council" feature that cross-checks answers across multiple LLMs, including the newly released Kimi K3.
news.means: Another agentic desktop tool is moving into everyday Office work, worth a bake-off before recommending a single-vendor agent stack.

news.body: Used bookstores report bulk buyers snapping up pre-2022, low-circulation books, widely believed to be AI labs sourcing clean, non-AI-generated training data. A US judge recently ruled that Anthropic's practice of buying and scanning books for training under its Project Panama program is fair use, as long as the books were legally acquired.
news.means: Legally-sourced training data now has real court backing, worth raising when a client asks due-diligence questions about where a vendor's model was trained.
